texts: The Weight of Ash Elara digs through the gray silt covering her cellar door. She finds her brother Elias's locket buried in the muck, crushed into the floorboards. The ash consumes metal and wood alike. Elias did not leave; he was buried where he stood.

Ashfall: The Gatekeeper Kael watches the gate from the shadows while the traveler ignores the warning signs. He sees the intruder pocket the iron key before the heavy doors groan open. The traveler does not know the gate requires a blood sacrifice to remain shut. Kael holds the burden of keeping the seal.

The Ashfall Gate Elias unearths a sealed iron trunk beneath the frozen soil of Ashfall. Instead of gold or secrets, the box contains a functioning, humming radio broadcasting his own voice from three days in the future. The Ashfall soil preserves sound. The future is mutable but predictable.

The Silent Offering Kael steps from the shadows. He offers his own palm to the traveler instead of seizing the key. The traveler hesitates, then presses their blade into Kael's skin to satisfy the lock. Kael intends to force the traveler to carry the burden of the seal.

The Price of Iron Kael steps from the alcove. His blade catches the dim light. He demands the traveler return the key before the gears lock. The traveler laughs and thrusts the iron into the slot. The gate mechanism reacts to human touch. Kael cannot stop the cycle once the key finds the hole.

The Price of Iron Kael lunges from the dark. He slams the traveler against the iron gate. The key in the traveler's hand slices Kael's palm. Blood coats the lock and the metal hums. The traveler stops moving as his own skin begins to turn to cold iron. The sacrifice does not have to be willing, and the gate consumes the intruder to seal itself.

The Gate Stalls The iron conversion reaches the traveler's shoulder, then stops. The gate trembles, failing to anchor the change, as the traveler's blood contains a strange, unnatural residue. Kael stares at the half-turned intruder, realizing the lock will not fully seal. The gate has a threshold for what it can consume; the traveler is defective in some way.

The Traveler's Final View Elara clutches the iron key, her fingers slick with sweat. She sees a shadow detach from the wall, but Kael is too fast. As he slams her against the gate, her desperate grip on the key slices his palm, feeding the lock she was desperate to open. Elara never intended to die; the sacrifice was an accident of her desperation.

The Gatekeeper's Debt Kael pulls the iron-skinned traveler from the lock. He drags the heavy body into the shadow of the gate. Kael cuts his own palm to drip fresh blood onto the stone floor instead of the gate itself. The seal hums but does not fully close. Kael can manipulate the sacrifice to save a life, but at a personal cost.

The Second Key Kael pulls the traveler back from the metal teeth of the gate. A second traveler steps from the fog behind Kael. This new arrival holds an identical iron key. The gate requires two sacrifices.

The Traveler's Weight The traveler watches his fingers harden into grey metal while Kael bleeds onto the lock. He realizes the gate feeds on bone to stay shut, and his own blood is payment enough. The traveler understands the sacrifice before he dies.

The Weight of the Seal Kael kneels beside the finished statue of iron. He strips the brass ring from the dead traveler's cold finger. The massive doors lock completely. Kael wears the ring and accepts the toll on his own blood. The gate takes a life but leaves a toll behind, and Kael must bear the personal cost of the seal.

The Weight of the Seal Kael kneels beside the iron statue of the traveler. He pries the iron key from the dead fingers. He opens the latch on his own chest instead of the gate. He forces the key into his ribs to keep the seal open. Kael uses his own body as the permanent anchor for the gate.

The Weight of the Seal Kael drops his knife. He drives the blade into his own shoulder to match the traveler's sacrifice. The heavy doors latch shut as the second drop of blood hits the iron floor. Kael falls against the metal frame. The gate demands blood from the keeper if the intruder lacks enough mass to finish the seal.

The Weight of the Seal Kael kneels by the iron-turned traveler. He pries the cold fingers apart to retrieve the key. The metal is freezing. Kael pockets the key and feels the first stiffness in his own bleeding hand. The sacrifice infection passes through contact with the key or the body.

prose The gate hums. Kael drops to his knees on the stone. He pries the iron key from the rigid fingers of the statue. The metal is grey. The traveler's boots remain leather. Kael hooks the latch on his own sternum. He pulls the iron plate back. He pushes the key deep into his ribs. The gate falls silent.

prose Kael pries the iron key from the dead fingers. The latch on his chest clicks open. The key meets the bone of his ribs. A second key sits inside the cavity already. The old key fuses to the new one. The gate hums louder. The doors do not lock.

prose The metal statue stays warm for three seconds. Kael grips the stiff fingers. Each joint clicks like an old latch. He bends the thumb back and pulls the iron key free. Blood drips from the key onto the stone floor. Kael reaches for his own ribs. He finds the small hatch beneath his collarbone. He clicks his fingernail into the groove and flips the iron plate open. The hollow sounds like an empty tin box. He pushes the key through his skin. The teeth find bone. He clicks the plate shut.
The Rib-Latch Kael forces his own ribs apart. The second key fits into the bone socket beside his heart. The metal latch clicks twice. Kael was always the backup mechanism for the gate.

The Second Key Inside the ash-choked watchtower, Vane listens to the heavy thud of Kael's boots on the stairs. Vane pulls a duplicate iron key from his pocket and drops it into the mortar dust. Kael enters with blood dripping from his palm and says nothing. Kael is not the only one holding an iron key.

The Second Key Kael pulls the second key from his own chest cavity. The brass teeth slide out of his ribs with a dry click. He holds it to the humming iron lock. The gate refuses the match. Kael's own key cannot shut the gate he just sealed.

The Weight in the Ribs Kael stands before the iron gate. He reaches into his open chest. He grips the second key beneath his ribs and pushes it deeper into the lock. Kael uses his own body to force the gate shut.

The Price in the Dust Vane steps from the shadows of the watchtower and kicks the iron key across the mortar dust. Kael looks down at the metal, then presses his bleeding palm against the stone floor. Vane draws a rusted blade and waits for Kael to answer. Vane demands Kael's second key by force.

The Empty Cavity Kael forces his hand into his own ribs. His fingers scrape against empty space. The second key is gone. Vane stands behind him on the stairs with the iron key in his palm. Vane stole the second key before Kael arrived.

prose Kael stands before the iron gate. Cold air strikes the meat of his chest. Bone splinters against the brass teeth of the key. Blood pools in the bottom of the lock. The metal turns red. The gate demands more weight.
prose Kael pushes the key. The iron tumbler grinds against the rib. The key snaps in two. The latch stays open.

prose Kael pushes the second key into the iron mouth of the gate. Bone grinds against cold brass inside his chest. The lock turns once. The bolt slides home. Kael leaves his hand inside the mechanism.

The Bone Rejects the Brass The key inside Kael's chest grinds against his ribs and snaps the brass teeth. The gate lock remains jammed. Vane watches from the shadows of the stairs. The second key cannot open the lock while broken.
The Second Turn Kael pulls his hand from the lock. He leaves the iron key embedded in the iron plate. He walks past Vane without speaking. Kael will not remove the key from his own chest.

The Iron Edge Kael forces his fingers deeper into the open cavity of his chest. Bone splinters against the cold brass of the second key. Blood wells over the rim of the metal and drips onto the floorboards. The physical cost of turning the key is immediate and bodily.

prose Kael pulls his bloody wrist free from the iron plate. The key stays wedged in the vertical slot. He steps over the mortar dust on the stair. Vane stands against the lime-washed wall. Kael ignores him. The floorboards sag under the weight of his boots.

prose Kael pulls his wrist from the iron mouth. The skin tears. The iron key stays wedged in the plate. Kael steps around Vane. Blood drips on the stone stair. Vane watches the key. Kael walks past the threshold into the grey rain.
prose Kael pulls his hand from the iron plate. Blood smears the cold metal. The key remains in the lock. Kael steps past Vane. Dust settles on the stairwell. Vane stares at the door.

Ashfall: The Empty Room Vane climbs the remaining stairs to the watchtower apex. He finds the iron lock empty. Kael sits on the stone bench outside in the grey rain, whetting a blade with a dry stone. The gate needs no key when the blood is gone.
The Second Lock Vane tests the gate. The iron key turns in the plate, but the second bolt does not move. Kael leaves the tower door open to the grey rain. Two keys are required to seal the gate.

Ashfall: The Grey Rain Kael walks into the grey rain. Vane picks up the second key from the mortar dust. Vane places the key into the open padlock on his own chest. The latch clicks shut. Vane drops dead on the stone stair. Kael watches the body turn to iron. The gate requires a sacrifice to stay locked, and Vane chose to pay the toll.

The Threshold Vane picks up the second key from the mortar dust. He inserts the brass tooth into his own palm. Kael stands in the grey rain and watches the threshold refuse to close. The gate requires a keeper's flesh, not an iron duplicate.

The Threshold Kael steps into the grey rain outside the watchtower. The rain hits his open chest cavity. Water pools in the empty bone. The iron key inside fuses tighter to his ribs. Kael falls to his knees in the mud. The grey rain reacts with Kael's open chest cavity.

The Threshold Vane picks up the second key from the mortar dust. He inserts the brass teeth into the secondary slot of the gate. Kael stands in the grey rain and watches the heavy bolt slide home. Vane knows how to work the lock.

The Chest Opens Vane reaches into his own torn coat. He pulls his ribs apart with grey fingers. He drops the second iron key onto the bloody stones. Kael stares at the open cavity in Vane's chest. Vane possesses the same internal mechanism as Kael.
The Iron Drop Vane picks up the iron key from the mortar dust. He inserts the key into the inner latch. The heavy watchtower door swings shut. Vane intends to lock Kael outside.

The Drip on the Stone Kael stands in the grey rain outside the threshold. He watches his palm bleed into the puddles. The blood matches the color of the water. Kael's blood does not wash away in the rain.
Vane Watches Vane stares at the mortar dust. He picks up the second key from the floor. He walks to the open gate and watches Kael vanish into the grey rain. Vane possesses the second key.

The Left Hand Vane kneels in the mortar dust. He picks up the second key from the floor. He presses the metal against his own chest. His ribcage yields to the iron. Vane carries the same internal mechanism as Kael.

The Chest's Empty Void Kael reaches inside his torn chest cavity to verify the second key. His fingers scrape empty bone. The second key is gone from his chest. Kael no longer possesses the second key.
prose Vane kneels in the mortar dust. He picks up the brass tooth from the floor. He presses the metal against his sternum. Bone splinters. The brass slides between his ribs and locks.
prose Vane kneels in the mortar dust. He lifts the brass tooth from the floor. He holds the cold metal to his breastbone. Bone cracks. The iron slips beneath his ribs.

prose Vane kneels in the mortar dust. His fingers close on the brass teeth. He pushes the key against his sternum. Bone cracks. The metal slips between the ribs and rests against his lungs. Vane breathes. Blood pools in the dust.

The Second Bolt Vane walks past Kael into the grey rain. He lifts the brass key from his own hand and presses it into the outer jamb. The door clicks shut behind them. Vane can lock the watchtower from the outside without Kael's consent.
The Second Plate Vane watches Kael leave. Blood coats the iron teeth in the door. Vane touches his own cold ribs. Vane tracks Kael's blood on the stone.

The Second Tooth Vane presses his thumb into his sternum. Metal clicks against bone. Vane pulls the second key from his own chest cavity and drops it into the puddle at Kael's boots. Vane also carries the second key inside his body.

prose Vane looks at the open door. Rain hits the stone sill. The iron teeth in the lock hold Kael's blood. Vane presses his fingers against his coat. Bone meets cold metal beneath the wool. He breathes. The second key grinds against his ribs.

prose The rain strikes the stone stair. Kael is a grey shape at the edge of the roof. Vane stands. Blood smears the iron bolt. He presses his palm to his ribs. The brass key shifts under his skin. The metal grates against bone. Vane breathes. He looks at the open door.

prose Kael leaves. His boots slap the wet stone. Vane watches the door frame stay wide. Rain hits the floor inside. Vane lifts a hand to his chest. Cold metal presses against his ribs. Blood runs down his palm. The iron teeth in the door rust in the damp air.

The Outer Sill Vane walks to the open watchtower door. Rain hits his face. Kael stands ten paces down the slate path. Water fills Kael's bootprints in the mud. Vane touches the wet wool of his coat over the second key. Neither man speaks. Vane follows Kael outside into the rain, abandoning the shelter of the tower.

The Floor Below Vane walks down the spiral stair. He leaves the open door behind him. He finds Kael sitting on the lower stone landing. Kael holds his torn palm against his knee. Vane stops two steps above him. Neither man speaks. Kael did not leave the tower. He cannot.

The Third Rib Vane reaches into his coat. He pulls the brass key from his sternum. Blood drips on the stone floor. Kael turns at the threshold. Kael pushes his fingers into his own chest. He pulls his second key free. Both keys drop into the mortar dust. The keys can leave their bodies.

The Open Threshold Kael stands outside in the grey rain. He pulls the brass tooth from his palm. He drops it into the deep mud. The water does not wash the blood from the metal. Kael abandons the key.

The Third Turn Vane forces his fingers into the lock plate. The internal brass tooth catches his tendon. He twists his wrist until the joint snaps. The heavy iron door swings an inch outward. Vane can force the second bolt by breaking his own wrist inside the mechanism.

The Weight of the Sill Vane looks down at his palm. Dried blood coats the brass tooth. He closes his hand into a tight fist. Metal bites into his flesh. Rain falls through the open door and strikes his boots. Vane feels the physical toll of the metal embedded in his chest.
The Heavy Step Kael walks into the grey rain. Water fills his boot prints in the mud. He turns his head back toward the open tower door. Kael does not flee far from the tower.

The Outer Sill Kael turns on the stone threshold. He reaches into his open coat. He presses his palm flat against the damp mortar beside the door. He leaves the key behind in the wall instead of taking it away. Kael leaves the second key embedded in the mortar of the threshold.

The Grey Sill Kael stands outside the watchtower door in the grey rain. He looks down at his torn palm. Cold water fills the open wound. The blood does not wash away. He turns his back on the open threshold. Kael keeps the wound open despite the rain.

The Cold Weight Vane sits on the stone step. He watches his palm bleed where the brass tooth entered. The rain cools the skin around the wound. Vane feels the physical cost of the key embedded in his chest.

The Outer Sill Kael walks down the stone path away from the watchtower. Rain fills his boot tracks. He reaches the outer gate and finds it chained. The watchtower has an outer perimeter that remains barred.

The Cold Threshold Kael walks through the grey rain away from the tower. Water fills the open wound in his palm. He does not wipe the blood away. He stops at the outer wall and stares into the fog. Kael keeps moving away from Vane without seeking shelter.

The Threshold Stone Kael does not walk away into the rain. He kneels on the wet stone outside the open door. He presses his palm into the mortar until the gap takes his blood. Kael cannot cross the threshold while the key remains inside Vane.
The Palm Vane presses his bleeding palm against the cold mortar of the threshold. He tests the dead lock with his bare fingers. The iron plate remains unmoving. Vane cannot force the gate open alone.
The Grey Threshold Kael steps through the open door into the grey rain. Water hits his torn palm. He does not look back at Vane. Kael leaves the watchtower entirely.

The Third Rib Vane cuts his palm on the inner latch. Kael returns through the rain and pushes the heavy door until the rusted hinges scream. Neither speaks. The gate requires both bloodlines to turn the latch.

The Third Rib Vane climbs the tower stair. The metal key grinds against his lung with every breath. He reaches the bell chamber and finds Kael sitting on the floor. Kael holds a rusted saw. The key cannot be removed from Vane's chest without cutting bone.

The Third Rib Vane drags his chest across the threshold stone. The brass key inside his sternum catches on the door frame. Kael returns from the rain. He pushes Vane back onto the mortar dust. The key inside Vane cannot pass the threshold while Kael stands outside.

The Third Rib Vane sits alone on the stone floor. He reaches into his coat. He touches the cold edge of the brass key lodged against his bone. Rain pools near his boot. Vane cannot remove the key from his chest.

The Third Rib Vane falls against the stone table. The key inside his chest grinds his lung. He pulls a rusted scalpel from the shelf. He cuts the third rib to release the metal. Blood pours onto the slate. Removing the key causes physical ruin.

The Third Rib Kael walks through the grey rain. Water pools in his torn palm. The brass tooth in his chest grinds against his collarbone with every stride. He looks back at the open door of the watchtower. Vane remains inside. Kael feels the metal inside his chest fighting his own bone.

The Third Rib Vane sits on the stone bench. He takes a rusted iron probe from his pocket. He slides the tip between his ribs, seeking the brass teeth. The metal grates against bone. Blood wells through his woolen tunic. He pulls the probe free and drops it into the mortar dust. Vane attempts to remove the foreign key himself.

The Mud Stair Kael walks down the stone steps outside the tower. Grey water fills his boot prints. He stops at the landing and presses his hand against his ribs. The brass tooth inside shifts against his lung. He turns back toward the open door. Kael cannot leave the tower's perimeter while the key remains inside his chest.

The Third Rib Vane stands at the open door. Rain hits the stone sill. Vane reaches into his coat. He touches the brass tooth lodged against his sternum. Blood leaks through his shirt. The metal turns one millimeter inside his flesh. The key inside Vane moves independently of his own muscle.
